title: Kelly's band during World War I: Marrero, Bond and drummers
summary: Barnes recalls Kelly's personnel in the First World War, including Lawrence Marrero on banjo and various drummers, and says he worked with many bands.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I don't tell you that. What about in World War I, who were you playing with? During the First World War? I played with Kelly. I played with Kelly.
Was that a big band or just a couple pieces? No, I would never use the most of the same pieces.
But you did use?
Yeah. Willie Foster was playing Brody in his band. You have a trombone? Yeah. And Harrison Bond.
Harrison Bond.
Harrison Bond. Yeah.
Was he good blues man? I don't know, there was no time on track. The moment was just enough. He may say when someone comes back.

Yes. Didn't want to be very tall. And he had a banjo? That was that boy? Lawrence. Lawrence Marrero. Lawrence Marrero. With Kelly. Anybody else? He's bass playing with Adam Marrero. So you had two Marrero's in the band. Yeah. One time I had two. Marrero in the fridge.
Sorry he was playing with. Sorry he played with Kelly too? Yeah. Well who usually played drums? I played drums with Kelly.
We had, he'd change up drums or someone.
We had this boy Happy. Which one? We had, he changed up them or so much. We had this boy, Happy. Which one? Benny.
Was it Red Happy or Black Happy? Red.
Red Happy. We had them down Benny. Benny. Benny.
Oh Benny. Black Benny?
Black Benny.
Black Benny. I had Dave Benny. Dave Benny. Yeah. Then again we had Hoogard.
Big O.
Big O.
Alex Big O. Yeah. But you weren't playing in any one spot now. You'd be playing different jobs, different places? I worked with different men and they had to catch me.
They'd tell me all the time, put a book, they'd go to Dayton.
